root_cause.text: A logic error in `fs/smb/client/smbdirect.c` caused `smbd_post_send_iter()` to free the `smbd_send_io` request after `smbd_send_batch_flush()` had already taken ownership and freed it, resulting in a double-free in the SMB Direct client send path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch comment states “`smbd_send_batch_flush()` already calls `smbd_free_send_io()`, so we should not call it again after `smbd_post_send()` moved it to the batch list,” and the diff adds a note that once the request is moved to the batch “we should not free it explicitly,” then changes the error path to `goto err_flush` to avoid the second `smbd_free_send_io(request)` call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ownership handling in batched send error cleanup to avoid freeing a request after it has been moved into the batch.
intent_record.what: The function `smbd_post_send_iter()` adds a comment stating that `request` is moved into `batch` and should not be freed explicitly after `smbd_post_send()` succeeds. It also introduces a `goto err_flush;` path after `smbd_send_batch_flush()` fails, and adds a new `err_flush:` label immediately before `err_alloc:` so the failure path skips `smbd_free_send_io(request)`.
intent_record.how: After a successful post-send, if batching is in use and the batch flush fails, the code now avoids freeing `request` twice because ownership has already been transferred to the batch. The new control flow preserves cleanup of credits and wakeup handling while preventing an incorrect explicit free on the flush-failure path.

candidates.rationale: This cleanup frees the request unconditionally on the error path even after ownership may have been transferred to smbd_send_batch_flush(), which can already free it, causing a double-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally frees the send request on the error path, even when ownership has already been transferred to smbd_send_batch_flush(). That creates a double-free when the batch flush path also frees the same smbd_send_io object.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable double-free is not present in this version. The root cause was that `smbd_post_send_iter()` would free the `smbd_send_io` request after `smbd_send_batch_flush()` had already taken ownership and freed it. In this snippet, the relevant cleanup is centralized in `smbd_free_send_io()`, and `send_done()` now calls `smbd_free_send_io(request);` directly instead of manually freeing the request after separate unmap/free steps. In `smbd_post_send_iter()`, the error path also uses `smbd_free_send_io(request);` instead of duplicating cleanup logic. The introduction of `smbd_alloc_send_io()` / `smbd_free_send_io()` and the comment `/* The list needs to be empty! The caller should take care of it. */` indicate ownership-aware cleanup, so the buggy construct is absent and the fix is already present.
